submitter: bugs_open/283 session (RFC_032 step 3 — retire the {{.ComponentID}} bindings)
rationale:
RFC_032 §8 (owner ruling 2026-08-22) is 'converge on {{.InstanceID}} and retire {{.ComponentID}}'. Step 2 (converting the templates) landed earlier today. This is the retirement itself: delete the render-context bindings so the placeholder cannot be used again.

WHY THE ORDER MATTERS, because it is the whole risk. The renderer runs with missingkey=zero, so a placeholder with no binding does not error — it renders EMPTY. A template still spelling id="{{.ComponentID}}" after this change renders id="", and the collision detector CANNOT SEE THAT: reElementID is `\sid="([^"{}]+)"` and the + requires at least one character. So the failure mode of deleting too early is an invalid page that every automated check reports as clean. This is not hypothetical — four idea.uk guide pages are serving <section id=""> today (written 2026-08-12), and one was fetched live to confirm it.

SO THE PRECONDITION IS ZERO, AND IT IS MEASURED. Census run before the deletion, across EVERY live table with a template-or-html column (a DO block over information_schema, not a guess at which table matters): the placeholder survives in exactly two places, content_components.html_template and component_versions.html_template. The latter is history and is supposed to hold it. The former held THREE rows, not the one the earlier is_active-filtered query showed: pricing (ACTIVE, 0 placements) plus header and footer (both INACTIVE, 0 placements, same 2025-11-21 library seed). All three are now converted and the count is 0.

WHY THOSE THREE COULD NOT GO THROUGH THE PIPELINE. The conversion files one work item per component and site_work_items.site_id is NOT NULL, while content_components has no site column — a template's site is only reachable through the pages that place it. With zero placements there is no honest site to file against, so the placement-driven seed skips them silently. They were converted by the REAL converter (ConvertTemplateToInstanceScope) and passed the REAL gate (GateConvertedTemplate) with a CONTROL proving the gate REFUSES each unconverted original; only the persistence is by hand, mirroring writeScopedTemplate exactly (snapshot to component_versions at MAX+1, then UPDATE, guarded on the row still spelling the placeholder). The two INACTIVE rows were converted deliberately: they cannot render today, but once the bindings are gone a reactivated row is exactly the invisible-empty-id case above.

THE SEED FILES ARE PART OF THE SAME HOLE. 247_mechanism_flow_component.sql and 250_evidence_timeseries_component.sql both create their component with id="{{.ComponentID}}" and both carry ON CONFLICT (name) DO UPDATE — and NEITHER is recorded in schema_migrations, so the runner's own pending test (filename not in the ledger, run-migrations.sh:225) treats them as pending. A migration run would replay them and overwrite two of the templates converted this morning, reinstating a placeholder nothing binds. Only the id line is changed in each, so every other replay hazard those files carry is left exactly as it was rather than quietly widened by me.

WHAT IS DELIBERATELY NOT IN THIS CHANGE. The THIRD binding, v3_site_actions.go:2385, is edited in the working tree but NOT committed. That file currently carries another session's uncommitted work (five further hunks: section-metadata carry keys, a changed applyWorkItemFailureLadder signature) which calls three functions defined in platform/orchestration/actions/section_metadata_keys.go — a file that is UNTRACKED and absent from HEAD. Committing the file by pathspec would take their half-finished work with mine and put calls to undefined symbols on the shared branch, breaking HEAD's build for every session. It is inert-safe to leave: with zero templates referencing the placeholder, a binding nothing reads changes no output. It is named here and in the lane docs so it is finished rather than forgotten.

plan.summary: Retire {{.ComponentID}}: delete the render-context binding on the rerender path and the dead substitution on the assemble path, and stop two unrecorded seed files from replaying the placeholder back into two templates. Precondition measured at zero across every live template column first. One third binding is deliberately left uncommitted because its file carries another session's WIP that would break HEAD.

component_instance_scope.go:215 — reElementID = `\sid="([^"{}]+)"`. The + is why an empty id is invisible to DetectInstanceCollisions, which is what makes deleting a binding too early a SILENT failure rather than a loud one.

plan.risks:
What a reviewer should check, in order.

1) IS THE PRECONDITION ACTUALLY ZERO? Everything here rests on it. The check is one line and it should be re-run rather than trusted: SELECT count(*) FROM content_components WHERE html_template LIKE '%ComponentID%'. It was 3 before this change and 0 after. If a reviewer can find a template source I did not census — a table whose column is not named like a template, a template held in jsonb, a file seeded outside sql_for_agents — that is the objection worth making, because my census was column-NAME driven and would miss exactly that.

2) THE THIRD BINDING IS STILL LIVE, ON PURPOSE. v3_site_actions.go:2385 still binds. That is stated in the rationale with the reason (another session's untracked WIP in the same file). A reviewer who thinks a partial retirement is worse than none should say so — my judgement is that it is inert (nothing reads the binding now) and that breaking HEAD's build for every session is the larger harm.

3) THE DETECTOR IS STILL BLIND TO id="". This change removes the CAUSE of the current empty ids, not the blindness. Any FUTURE cause of an empty id still passes every check. That is a detector fix with its own blast radius across every DetectInstanceCollisions caller and it stays in RFC_032's track — named, not silently deferred.

4) THE FOUR LIVE EMPTY-ID PAGES ARE NOT REPAIRED BY THIS CHANGE. They hold stored HTML written on 2026-08-12; their re-render items already read 'complete' without rewriting those rows. Fixing the cause does not repair the casualties, and the casualties are named rather than assumed to heal.

5) THE INACTIVE ROWS. Converting header/footer touches rows nothing renders. The alternative was to leave two reactivation hazards behind a change whose whole point is that the placeholder can never render empty again. If a reviewer would rather have deactivated-and-deleted them, that is a real option I did not take, because deleting library rows is not this change's mandate.
